roadmap.notes: OPERATING MODEL: 18 acceptance scenarios (cdo01-cdo18, no cdo12-omission -- cdo12 exists, numbering is contiguous cdo01-cdo18) across 2 crates (embyr-db-prep, embyr-server) + 2 shared crates (embyr-core, embyr-pg-storage), per DISTILL's Scenario List and Adapter Coverage Table (docs/feature/customer-db-onboarding/feature-delta.md, DISTILL section). For each step below, un-ignore the scenario(s) named in scenario_name ONE AT A TIME (cdo01 and cdo12 are the two @walking_skeleton scenarios, already non-#[ignore] and already RED; all other cdo0N are #[ignore]), implement just enough of the named production symbol(s) to make it pass, then run the FULL cdo01..cdo18 suite (not just the one test) before committing -- several later scenarios reuse fixture helpers/production code paths earlier steps establish and a regression there is cheap to catch immediately. GROUPING RATIONALE (deviates from DISTILL's own US-01(11)/US-02(7) split where a shared implementation unit or cross-cutting production dependency made a different grouping more honest -- flagged explicitly per this task's dispatch instruction): (1) cdo01/cdo02/cdo03 land together in 01-01 because they are one implementation unit -- a single before/after count of `_sqlx_migrations` rows around one `PostgresBackendAdapter::migrate()` call classifies fresh-apply vs. no-op vs. resume; sqlx's own migrator is already idempotent/resumable (DISTILL's own note), so no scenario-specific branching is needed. (2) cdo04/cdo05 land together in 01-02 because both are `error_report::classify()` output-shape scenarios sharing one function. (3) cdo06 (02-01) is its own step -- a structural/architecture-enforcement scenario (grep-based, no runtime behavior) touching entirely different files (embyr-server/provision.rs, embyr-pg-storage/backend_adapter.rs) than every other step, and is a HARD PREREQUISITE for 03-01 -- see FUNCTION-CALL DEPENDENCY TRACE below. (4) cdo12/cdo16/cdo18 land together in 03-01 because all three exercise the identical `SchemaReadiness::Ready` code path (verify_schema_readiness() Ready variant + provision.rs's Ready-skip-migrate branch); cdo18 additionally locks the `>=` (not `==`) comparison this same implementation must get right the first time, so it is proving 03-01's logic, not requesting new logic. (5) cdo13/cdo14/cdo15/cdo17 land together in 04-01 because all four exercise the identical 'enrich, don't replace, the existing migrate-attempt failure path' branch (CDO-AD-04) -- cdo15 and cdo17 add zero new production code beyond what cdo13/cdo14 require (cdo15 cross-checks cdo13's error field against the pre-existing, unchanged `backend_unavailable` path; cdo17 cross-checks that the pre-existing auto-migrate-success path is untouched) but are kept in the SAME step as the code that makes them pass, not split into a separate validation-only step. (6) cdo07/cdo08/cdo09/cdo10/cdo11 land together in 05-01 (5 scenarios, under the 8-scenario flag threshold) because all five exercise the SAME two new adapter methods (discover_current_user, grant_schema_readiness_read) plus main.rs's DML-role-DSN branch -- cdo08 (negative/PUBLIC-regression), cdo10 (idempotency), and cdo11 (injection-safety) are proof properties of cdo07's implementation, not separate implementation units; cdo09 (OQ-5 sequencing) was DISTILL-grouped into this same block (not split into its own step) specifically to avoid a validation-only step, since its 3-step chained journey needs both 03-01's verify_schema_readiness() (already done, see dependency below) and 05-01's own grant methods and adds no code beyond correct informational-message wording in the DML-DSN-absent branch that 01-01/01-02 already establish. STEP COUNT: 7 (vs. DISTILL's implicit 11+7=18 if 1:1'd to scenario groups) -- decomposition ratio 7 steps / 6 production files (crates/embyr-db-prep/src/{main.rs,config.rs,error_report.rs}, crates/embyr-core/src/domain/schema_readiness.rs, crates/embyr-pg-storage/src/backend_adapter.rs, crates/embyr-server/src/admin/handlers/provision.rs) = 1.17, well under the 2.5 ceiling. Max scenarios in any single step is 5 (05-01), under the 8-scenario flag threshold -- no step flagged. FUNCTION-CALL DEPENDENCY TRACE (done before assignment, per this dispatch's explicit instruction): `PostgresBackendAdapter::verify_schema_readiness()` (implemented in 03-01) MUST read the highest expected migration version from the SAME `sqlx::migrate!("../../migrations/customer")` embed `migrate()` uses -- cdo06's own architecture-enforcement test (grep-based, scans the literal macro-invocation string workspace-wide) permits exactly ONE occurrence anywhere in crates/, so 03-01 CANNOT add a second independent macro call to learn the expected version. This means 02-01 (which already touches backend_adapter.rs to collapse provision.rs's 3 inline macro calls + refactor run_migrations() to delegate to migrate()) must ALSO hoist the macro invocation out of migrate()'s method body into a module-level `static MIGRATOR: sqlx::migrate::Migrator = sqlx::migrate!("../../migrations/customer");` in backend_adapter.rs, so both migrate() and verify_schema_readiness() (03-01) read the identical static -- 02-01 is therefore a HARD PREREQUISITE of 03-01, not merely a nearby concern (dependencies reflect this). Confirmed via grep before this roadmap was written: `PostgresBackendAdapter::run_migrations(pool)` (the static convenience 02-01 refactors to delegate to migrate()) has exactly 2 external call sites workspace-wide, both in tests/acceptance/embyr_agent/{mod.rs,us_a05_subscribe.rs} -- unrelated to this feature, signature-compatible, unaffected by the internal delegation refactor. Separately, cdo09 (05-01) directly constructs a `PostgresBackendAdapter` and calls `.verify_schema_readiness()` on it inside the TEST BODY itself (not through main.rs) to assert the NotPrepped-then-Ready transition -- this is a hard dependency of 05-01 on 03-01 having already landed a real (non-panicking) verify_schema_readiness(), reflected in 05-01's dependencies. No step calls a function scheduled for implementation in a LATER step. PBT NOTE: 03-01 is the one step introducing new pure-function logic (the SchemaReadiness comparison, `found_version >= expected_version` in embyr-core) -- flagged in its own implementation_notes as this feature's PBT-appropriate surface per Mandate 9/CM-F, using Rust's `proptest` (this project's Hypothesis-equivalent, already a workspace dev-dependency per docs/architecture/atdd-infrastructure-policy.md) rather than a literal Python Hypothesis translation, since embyr-rs is a Rust codebase (CLAUDE.md: functional-where-practical Rust paradigm). Every other step's acceptance-level tests are layer-3 (real subprocess + real testcontainers Postgres) and are explicitly EXEMPT per Mandate 9 (example-only at that layer) -- each step's implementation_notes states the exemption and reason individually rather than pasting the Hypothesis-specific mandate paragraph verbatim into a Rust-only codebase where it would be misleading. Mutation gate: cargo-mutants -p embyr-core --filter schema_readiness (ADR-023 Enforcement) targets 03-01's pure logic specifically -- per-feature mutation gate per project CLAUDE.md.

phases.name: US-01: embyr-db-prep Core Migrate-and-Report Flow + Error Classification (Slice 01)

steps.name: Walking Skeleton (US-01) -- DbPrepConfig::from_env() + main.rs core migrate-and-report flow (fresh apply, idempotent no-op, interrupted-run resume)
criteria: Running embyr-db-prep against a fresh, reachable, sufficiently-privileged database applies the full expected migration set and reports success naming the schema version applied, exit code 0 (AC-01-01)
Re-running against an already-fully-prepared database makes no further schema changes and reports 'already up to date' (AC-01-02)

Re-running after an interrupted partial run (only migration 0001 previously applied via sqlx's own Migrate trait) resumes from the last successfully-applied migration, completes without duplicate-object errors, and reports the same 'ready' confirmation as a clean first-time run (AC-01-03)

DbPrepConfig::from_env() reads EMBYR_DB_PREP_DSN (required) and EMBYR_DB_PREP_DML_ROLE_DSN (optional) and returns Err naming the missing variable when EMBYR_DB_PREP_DSN is absent/empty, mirroring AgentConfig::from_env()'s error-accumulation pattern

When EMBYR_DB_PREP_DML_ROLE_DSN is absent, main.rs prints an informational (non-error) note that read-verification access was not established, without attempting any grant-related call (stubs the branch 05-01 fills in; must not panic)
steps.implementation_notes: Replace two RED panics. config.rs DbPrepConfig::from_env() (panic: 'DbPrepConfig::from_env: not yet implemented -- RED scaffold'): mirror AgentConfig::from_env()'s collect_required/error-accumulation shape (crates/embyr-agent/src/config.rs) but simpler -- only EMBYR_DB_PREP_DSN is required; EMBYR_DB_PREP_DML_ROLE_DSN is read via std::env::var(...).ok().filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) into dml_role_dsn: Option<String>, no accumulation needed for an optional var. main.rs (currently just calls from_env() and discards the panic): (1) call from_env(), on Err print to stderr and std::process::exit(1); (2) connect a PgPoolOptions pool to cfg.dsn (timeout-bound, mirror StartupProbe's tokio::time::timeout wrapping in crates/embyr-agent/src/probe.rs -- full connection-failure classification is 01-02's scope, this step only needs the happy-reachable path to work without hanging); (3) construct PostgresBackendAdapter::new(&cfg.dsn) (already-real constructor) or reuse the pool from step 2 via new_from_pool(pool); (4) BEFORE calling migrate(), query `SELECT count(*) FROM _sqlx_migrations WHERE success` on the adapter's pool, treating a 'relation does not exist' error as 0 (fresh DB, table not yet created) -- this is the before-count; (5) call adapter.migrate() (already real, unchanged in this step -- do not touch its internals here, that is 02-01's scope) and on Err delegate to a placeholder path this step does not need to make presentable yet (01-02 fills in classify()); (6) on Ok, query the same count again (after-count, table now guaranteed to exist since migrate() creates it) -- if before == after and before > 0, print an 'already up to date' message (satisfies cdo02); otherwise print a 'database ready for embyr onboarding (schema version {after} of {after} applied)' message (satisfies cdo01 fresh-apply and cdo03 resume, both of which have before != after); (7) if cfg.dml_role_dsn is None, print the informational grant-skipped note (exact wording checked more precisely by cdo09 in 05-01, but establish it now so 01-01's own tests are unaffected either way); if Some, this step may leave a TODO comment -- do not call discover_current_user()/grant_schema_readiness_read() yet, they still panic until 05-01; (8) exit 0 on success. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: all 3 scenarios in this step are layer-3 acceptance tests (real embyr-db-prep subprocess + real testcontainers Postgres, per DISTILL's Two-Tier Acceptance Decision and Mandate Compliance Evidence CM-F) -- example-based per Mandate 9, not a Hypothesis/property-based-test candidate at this layer. No new pure-function logic is introduced by this step (the before/after count comparison is a thin I/O-bound helper, not a candidate for extraction) so there is no adjacent unit-level PBT slot to compensate with here; see 03-01's implementation_notes for this feature's actual PBT-appropriate surface.

steps.name: US-01 error classification -- error_report::classify() + main.rs wiring for insufficient-privilege and unreachable-host failures
criteria: A privilege-insufficient login produces a message naming the missing privilege and the target database/role, not a raw driver error or panic stack trace, and the tool exits non-zero (AC-01-04)
An unreachable target host produces a connection-failure message, distinguishable in content from an insufficient-privilege message, and the tool exits non-zero (AC-01-05)
steps.implementation_notes: Replace one RED panic and extend 01-01's main.rs error branches. error_report.rs classify(err: &CoreError) -> String (panic: 'error_report::classify: not yet implemented -- RED scaffold'): match on CoreError variants/wrapped SQLSTATE -- a CoreError::PermissionDenied(_) or a BackendUnavailable(msg) whose inner sqlx error carries SQLSTATE 42501 (insufficient_privilege) formats as 'insufficient privilege: role <role> lacks CREATE on database <db>' using the role/database names parsed from cfg.dsn's own components (never from server error-message content, per the Earned Trust probe design table's convention of not trusting substrate-supplied text for identity) -- any other BackendUnavailable is the generic fallback message. main.rs's connectivity-probe step (01-01's step 2, currently a bare timeout-wrapped connect) must be restructured so a CONNECT-PHASE failure (before any query reaches Postgres -- i.e., the pool never opens, or the SELECT 1 probe itself times out/fails to connect) short-circuits to a DISTINCT, hardcoded 'connection failed: <host> unreachable' message and exit(1) WITHOUT ever calling classify() or attempting migrate() -- this is what makes AC-01-05's message structurally impossible to contain 'privilege'/'permission denied' (cdo05 asserts this negative). A migrate()-phase failure (pool connected fine, SELECT 1 succeeded, but migrate() itself errors) is the only path that reaches classify(). Wire the two error paths in main.rs to print classify()'s result (migrate-phase) or the hardcoded connection message (connect-phase) to stderr before exit(1). EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: both scenarios are layer-3 acceptance tests (real subprocess against a deliberately-unreachable RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1 address and a deliberately-unprivileged real Postgres role) -- example-based per Mandate 9. classify()'s SQLSTATE-branching logic is a plausible future PBT candidate (enumerate SQLSTATE space x message-shape invariants) but DISTILL's own scenario list only requires 2 named message shapes plus a generic fallback -- adding proptest machinery for a 3-arm match is not proportionate at this scope; compensate, if this classification logic grows a 4th+ arm in a future feature, with a proptest suite over the SQLSTATE enum at that time.

phases.name: Migration Embed Consolidation (ADR-022) -- single sqlx::migrate! embed point workspace-wide

steps.name: Collapse provision.rs's 3 inline sqlx::migrate! embeds + backend_adapter.rs's run_migrations() to the single migrate() embed point (ADR-022)
criteria: Exactly one occurrence of the literal `sqlx::migrate!("../../migrations/customer")` invocation exists anywhere under crates/ workspace-wide (currently 5: 3 in provision.rs's branches, 2 in backend_adapter.rs's migrate()/run_migrations())

The sole surviving occurrence lives in crates/embyr-pg-storage/src/backend_adapter.rs, hoisted to a module-level static so both migrate() and (in step 03-01) verify_schema_readiness() read the identical compiled-in Migrator
provision.rs's aws_secret, gcp_secret, and direct_pg branches all apply migrations by calling PostgresBackendAdapter's migrate() method against the already-open customer_pool, not the macro directly

run_migrations(pool) delegates internally to an adapter instance's migrate() rather than invoking the macro a second time; its public signature and behavior are unchanged for its 2 existing external callers (tests/acceptance/embyr_agent/mod.rs, tests/acceptance/embyr_agent/us_a05_subscribe.rs -- confirmed via grep, unrelated to this feature, unaffected by this internal refactor)
steps.implementation_notes: Pure refactor, no new scaffolds to remove (migrate() already works). backend_adapter.rs: move `sqlx::migrate!("../../migrations/customer")` out of migrate()'s body into a module-level `static MIGRATOR: sqlx::migrate::Migrator = sqlx::migrate!("../../migrations/customer");` (or an equivalent once-only binding sqlx's macro supports at module scope); migrate() becomes `MIGRATOR.run(&self.pool).await.map_err(...)`; run_migrations(pool: &PgPool) becomes `Self::new_from_pool(pool.clone()).migrate().await` (new_from_pool already exists, takes ownership of a PgPool -- PgPool is an Arc-backed handle, .clone() is cheap) -- this keeps run_migrations()'s existing `&PgPool` signature for its 2 external callers while eliminating its independent macro call. provision.rs: in each of the 3 branches (aws_secret ~line 168, gcp_secret ~line 220, direct_pg ~line 351), replace the inline `sqlx::migrate!("../../migrations/customer").run(&customer_pool).await...` with `embyr_pg_storage::backend_adapter::PostgresBackendAdapter::new_from_pool(customer_pool.clone()).migrate().await.map_err(|e| err(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, &e.to_string()))?` (or equivalent, preserving each branch's existing error-status mapping -- direct_pg's branch currently migrates AFTER the projects INSERT/commit, aws_secret/gcp_secret migrate BEFORE; preserve each branch's existing ordering exactly, this step changes only the migration invocation mechanism, not call ordering, since 03-01/04-01 depend on today's ordering being otherwise stable). This step is a hard prerequisite for 03-01 (see roadmap notes' Function-Call Dependency Trace) -- verify_schema_readiness() must read the SAME static MIGRATOR this step creates, not a second macro invocation, or cdo06 regresses. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: the single scenario here is a structural/architecture-enforcement test (grep-based scan of real workspace source files, no runtime behavior, no Postgres, no subprocess) -- not a Hypothesis/property-based-test candidate; there is no adjacent runtime invariant to state-delta against, only a static-count assertion already fully specified by the test itself.

phases.name: US-02: Schema-Readiness Verification + Ready-Path Provisioning (ADR-023 core mechanism)

steps.name: Walking Skeleton (US-02) -- SchemaReadiness comparison logic + PostgresBackendAdapter::verify_schema_readiness() + provision.rs Ready-skip-migrate branch (forward-compatible >= comparison)
criteria: Provisioning with a DML-only connection string against a fully-prepped database succeeds and returns the standard {project_id, api_key} response (AC-02-01)

Provisioning succeeds against a fully-prepped database without embyr's provisioning flow requiring or attempting any elevated (DDL) privilege on the submitted connection string -- verify_schema_readiness() is SELECT-only against _sqlx_migrations, and migrate() is never invoked on the Ready path (AC-02-05)

A database whose _sqlx_migrations bookkeeping shows found_version > expected_version (a newer prep-tool build than this server's compiled-in Migrator) is treated as Ready, not Stale or blocked -- not strict equality (OQ-1/CDO-AD-05)

verify_schema_readiness() reads sqlx's own _sqlx_migrations table (no new table type) and compares the highest successfully-applied version against 02-01's compiled-in MIGRATOR's own highest embedded version
steps.implementation_notes: Replace one RED panic and extend one already-real function. schema_readiness.rs currently has zero behavior (a pure enum with doc comments only, per DISTILL's own note it is 'not scaffold-panicked -- pure data type, no behavior to RED') -- add a pure comparison function here, e.g. `pub fn classify(found_version: i64, expected_version: i64, missing_tables: Vec<String>) -> SchemaReadiness`: found_version <= 0 (table absent/unreadable is the caller's concern, represented upstream as found_version=0) -> NotPrepped{missing_tables}; 0 < found_version < expected_version -> Stale{expected_version, found_version}; found_version >= expected_version -> Ready{schema_version: found_version} (NOT strict equality -- this is OQ-1/CDO-AD-05's forward-compatible boundary, cdo18 locks it). backend_adapter.rs verify_schema_readiness() (panic: 'PostgresBackendAdapter::verify_schema_readiness: not yet implemented -- RED scaffold'): `SELECT version, success FROM _sqlx_migrations ORDER BY version` against self.pool (SELECT-only, AC-02-05) -- on a relation-does-not-exist error (or zero rows / any success=false), pass found_version=0 to schema_readiness::classify() with missing_tables naming 'documents'/'transactions' (ADR-023 Alternative 3's retained diagnostic-only role for table-presence, not the versioning source of truth); otherwise take the highest version where success=true and compare against 02-01's static MIGRATOR.migrations.last().version (or .len() given contiguous 0001/0002 numbering) as expected_version. provision.rs's direct_pg branch (~line 311 onward): after the existing probe_customer_db() call, call verify_schema_readiness() on an adapter constructed from customer_pool; on Ready, SKIP the migrate() call entirely (proceed straight to the existing project INSERT/tx.commit()) -- this is what makes AC-02-05 true: migrate() is never invoked at all on the Ready path, not merely that it would fail harmlessly. On NotPrepped/Stale, fall through to today's existing migrate()-then-insert behavior UNCHANGED in this step (04-01's scope is enriching that failure path's error body; this step must not alter it beyond what's needed to make cdo12/16/18 pass -- do not add customer_db_not_prepped/customer_db_schema_stale response bodies yet, that would be 04-01's code landing early and untested here). PBT NOTE (this feature's PBT-appropriate surface, per Mandate 9/CM-F and this dispatch's own flag): add proptest-based property tests in crates/embyr-core for schema_readiness::classify() directly -- e.g. `proptest! { fn ready_iff_found_gte_expected(found in 0i64..1000, expected in 1i64..1000) { let result = classify(found, expected, vec![]); prop_assert_eq!(matches!(result, SchemaReadiness::Ready{..}), found >= expected); } }` plus a boundary-inclusive case (found == expected must be Ready, never Stale) and a found=0 case (always NotPrepped regardless of expected). This is the Rust-workspace equivalent of the skill's Hypothesis-@given mandate for this step's one piece of genuinely pure, comparison-shaped logic; it is what cargo-mutants -p embyr-core --filter schema_readiness (ADR-023 Enforcement) will exercise. The 3 layer-3 acceptance scenarios in this step (cdo12, cdo16, cdo18) remain EXEMPT/example-based per Mandate 9 -- they verify real-Postgres wiring end-to-end, not the pure invariant, which the proptest suite above covers directly.

phases.name: US-02: Provisioning Error Enrichment + Regression Guardrail (ADR-023 error paths, CDO-AD-04)

steps.name: provision.rs direct_pg branch -- enrich (not replace) the existing migrate-attempt failure path with customer_db_not_prepped / customer_db_schema_stale bodies
criteria: Provisioning against a database with no embyr schema present fails 400, naming the specific missing schema element (documents/transactions), not a generic backend_unavailable (AC-02-02)
Provisioning against a database with a stale schema version fails 400, naming both the expected schema version and the version found (AC-02-03)

The 'not ready' failure response ('customer_db_not_prepped'/'customer_db_schema_stale') is distinguishable, in its error field content, from a plain connectivity failure ('backend_unavailable', unchanged) to the target database (AC-02-04)
Existing full-privilege-DSN provisioning against a not-yet-prepped database continues to succeed via the unchanged automatic-migration path -- no regression (AC-02-06)
steps.implementation_notes: No RED panics remain in this file's scaffolding -- this step extends 03-01's already-real verify_schema_readiness()-call branch with the NotPrepped/Stale arms. On NotPrepped or Stale (03-01 already falls through to the existing migrate()-then-insert flow, unchanged): attempt the EXISTING, unchanged PostgresBackendAdapter::migrate() call (now via 02-01's adapter method, not a macro) exactly as today. If migrate() SUCCEEDS (the DML-only-looking DSN actually had DDL rights after all, e.g. AC-02-06's full-privilege regression case) -> proceed to the existing project INSERT exactly as today, UNCHANGED (this is what makes cdo17 pass with zero additional branching -- CDO-AD-04's 'enrich, don't replace' framing means the success path needs no new code at all). If migrate() FAILS -> instead of the current generic `err(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, &e.to_string())`, branch on the verify_schema_readiness() result captured earlier in this same request: NotPrepped{missing_tables} -> 400 with body `{"error": "customer_db_not_prepped", "detail": "table '<missing_tables[0]>' not found -- run the embyr database-preparation step first"}` (or naming all missing tables, cdo13 only asserts detail contains 'documents' or 'transactions'); Stale{expected_version, found_version} -> 400 with body `{"error": "customer_db_schema_stale", "detail": "expected schema version <expected_version>, found <found_version> -- re-run the embyr database-preparation step"}` (cdo14 asserts detail contains both '2' and '1'). AC-02-04/cdo15 needs no new code beyond the above -- it only cross-checks that this branch's error field ('customer_db_not_prepped') differs from probe_customer_db()'s pre-existing, unchanged 'backend_unavailable' (a genuinely-unreachable-host case never reaches verify_schema_readiness() at all, since probe_customer_db() already fails first). EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: all 4 scenarios are layer-3 acceptance tests (real embyr-server subprocess, real HTTP via reqwest, real testcontainers Postgres seeded into exactly the NotPrepped/Stale states via sqlx's own Migrate trait, per DISTILL's Adapter Coverage Table) -- example-based per Mandate 9. No new pure-function logic is introduced by this step (the error-body construction is a thin match-and-format, not a candidate for extraction); 03-01's schema_readiness::classify() proptest suite already covers the underlying NotPrepped/Stale boundary logic this step's error bodies merely report.

phases.name: US-01: DML-Role Grant Mechanism (ADR-023 revised, security-review resolution)

steps.name: discover_current_user() + grant_schema_readiness_read() + main.rs DML-role-DSN wiring (positive grant, PUBLIC-grant regression guard, idempotency, injection-safety, OQ-5 sequencing)
criteria: After a prep run supplies EMBYR_DB_PREP_DML_ROLE_DSN, the named DML role can SELECT * FROM _sqlx_migrations -- the grant is performed automatically, not by any test fixture (ADR-023 enforcement)

A second, distinct role never named to embyr-db-prep CANNOT read _sqlx_migrations (permission denied) -- the grant is role-scoped, not GRANT ... TO PUBLIC; this is the exact test that would have caught the original PUBLIC-grant proposal (security-review-specific negative test)

Running the full flow (migrate + discover + grant) twice against the same database and the same DML-role DSN is a no-op on the second run -- migrate()'s existing idempotency plus grant_schema_readiness_read()'s idempotency (re-granting an already-granted privilege is a Postgres no-op)

A DML role name containing a reserved Postgres keyword (e.g. `select`) is quoted correctly via Postgres's own format('%I', ...) and the grant still applies to it -- not hand-rolled Rust-side identifier quoting (injection-safety)

When EMBYR_DB_PREP_DML_ROLE_DSN is absent, migration success is still reported via the unchanged success message, an informational (non-error) grant-skipped note is printed, and a subsequent verify_schema_readiness() call (as a DML-only role that was never granted) reports NotPrepped rather than erroring unhandled -- until a follow-up prep run supplies the DSN and closes the gap (OQ-5 sequencing)
steps.implementation_notes: Replace two RED panics and complete 01-01's stubbed DML-role branch in main.rs. backend_adapter.rs discover_current_user() (panic: 'PostgresBackendAdapter::discover_current_user: not yet implemented -- RED scaffold'): `SELECT current_user` on self.pool, return the single string, then let the pool drop -- the caller (main.rs) constructs this adapter from EMBYR_DB_PREP_DML_ROLE_DSN specifically for this one call, mirroring StartupProbe's 'never log the DSN, only carry the derived value forward' convention (crates/embyr-agent/src/probe.rs). grant_schema_readiness_read(role_name: &str) (panic: 'PostgresBackendAdapter::grant_schema_readiness_read: not yet implemented -- RED scaffold', called against the ELEVATED adapter/pool, the owner of _sqlx_migrations): two round trips exactly as ADR-023 Mechanism step 4 specifies -- `SELECT format('%I', $1::text)` bound to role_name to obtain a safely-quoted identifier, THEN interpolate (not bind -- GRANT has no bind-parameter form) that quoted identifier into a plain `GRANT SELECT ON _sqlx_migrations TO <quoted>` statement executed via sqlx::query(&format!(...)).execute(&self.pool). Do NOT hand-roll Rust-side identifier escaping -- the entire point of this method (and cdo11) is delegating quoting to Postgres's own trusted format('%I', ...). main.rs: complete the `if let Some(dml_dsn) = &cfg.dml_role_dsn { ... }` branch 01-01 stubbed -- open a brief connection via PostgresBackendAdapter::new(dml_dsn) (timeout-bound, best-effort: on connect failure, treat identically to the DSN-absent case, printing the same informational skip note rather than hard-failing the whole run, since the migration itself already succeeded), call discover_current_user() on it to get role_name, drop that connection, then call grant_schema_readiness_read(role_name) on the ORIGINAL elevated adapter from step 1, and print a confirmation. This entire branch is naturally idempotent (cdo10) because GRANT re-application is a Postgres no-op and migrate() is already idempotent -- no new idempotency-guard code is needed beyond calling the same sequence unconditionally on every run when the DSN is present. cdo09's 3-step chained journey needs no new production code beyond what this step + 03-01 already deliver: step 1 (no DML DSN) exercises 01-01/05-01's informational-skip branch; step 2 constructs a PostgresBackendAdapter directly in the TEST body and calls verify_schema_readiness() (03-01, already real) as an ungranted role, expecting NotPrepped; step 3 re-runs embyr-db-prep WITH the DSN, exercising this step's grant branch, then re-calls verify_schema_readiness() expecting Ready -- confirm the exact informational-note wording from 01-01 satisfies cdo09's `contains("not established") || (contains("grant") && contains("skip"))` assertion; adjust wording here if 01-01's phrasing does not already match, rather than deferring to a separate step. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: all 5 scenarios are layer-3 acceptance tests (real embyr-db-prep subprocess, real testcontainers Postgres, real distinctly-privileged roles created by the test fixture) -- example-based per Mandate 9. The reserved-word-quoting property (cdo11) is a plausible PBT candidate in the abstract (generate arbitrary role-name strings, assert the GRANT always round-trips) but the actual quoting correctness is delegated entirely to Postgres's own format('%I', ...) by design (this method's whole purpose is to NOT reimplement identifier-quoting logic in Rust) -- there is no Rust-side pure function here to property-test; the property genuinely lives in Postgres's own (already-trusted, out-of-scope) implementation, which is why this scenario is a single pathological-example acceptance test rather than a PBT target.
